---
title: "Before you come"
---

Do these steps before the workshop. The room's wifi may be slow, so download and install at home. The whole setup takes about 15 minutes, most of it the package install.

## What to bring

- A laptop you can install software on.
- Optional: a dataset of your own with one row per individual, a 0/1 treatment column, a site or cluster identifier, a few covariates, and an outcome. The last block of the Chapter 5 page is a template for pointing the code at it. Nothing in the workshop requires it.

## What to have installed

1. **R 4.3 or later.** <https://cran.r-project.org>
2. **RStudio or Positron.** Either one. Both include Quarto, which you need only if you want to render the documents rather than run the chunks.
3. **This repository.** Either clone it or download the zip from the green Code button at <https://github.com/alberto-guzman/multilevel-matching-workshop> and unzip it. Open the folder as a project.
4. **The packages.** Open `00_install_packages.R` and run it. It installs 15 packages from CRAN. Say yes if asked to install from source.
5. **The check.** Open `00_check_setup.R` and run it. It should end with a line like `MatchIt test run: matched 710 students`. If it reports a missing package or an error, bring the output with you and we will fix it at the start.

## What to know

- Basic R, meaning running a script, reading a data frame, and the pipe. The code uses tidyverse verbs (`filter`, `mutate`, `summarise`) throughout.
- The ideas from the first hour of the workshop, which are potential outcomes, the propensity score, and what a standardized mean difference is. Chapters 1 to 3 of the handbook cover them if you want to read ahead.

## If the install fails

Every output in every document is already on this site, so you can follow on screen without running anything. Fix the install afterwards and the documents will run at home.
